nt in the Session, ArrowDown restores your draft.
# dsh-composer-input-history
Shell-style input history for the DeepSeek Harness Web composer — the behaviour you know from openco
de and other terminal agents.

> Press ↑ in the composer to pull back a message you already sent in this Session.
> Press ↓ to walk

forward again; past the newest message your original draft comes back,
> and one more ↓ discards it
and clears the composer.
## What it does
| Gesture | Behaviour |

| ↑ with an empty draft | recalls the newest sent message |
| ↑ again | walks one message older each

time |
| ↑ on the first line of a single-line draft | recalls; the draft you were writing is rememb

ered |
| ↑ inside a multi-line draft, below the first line | left to the editor, so the caret still

moves |
| ↓ while browsing | walks one message newer |
| ↓ past the newest message | restores the dr

aft you were writing before browsing |
| ↓ again, after the draft came back | discards the draft and

clears the composer |
| typing anything while browsing | leaves browse mode; the recalled text beco

oser |
| typing anything while browsing | leaves browse mode; the recalled text becomes your draft |
History is what you sent in this Session, oldest to newest, read from the Chat node store the view i
tself renders (`snapshot.nodes`, ordered by anchor sequence): ordinary user messages, steering messa
ges, and the message that woke a turn. Skipped: hidden nodes (compacted or interrupted), attachment-
only messages, and everything the Harness authors on your behalf — goal rounds, skill catalogs, runt
ime snapshots, job notices, model notices, approval answers, and compaction checkpoints. The visible
window is also persisted per Session in `localStorage` (capped at 300 entries) and merged with the
live store, so messages a compaction pruned stay recallable, including after a restart.
## Why it is a keyboard observer
The Harness composer deliberately leaves ↑/↓ to its shell-owned Lexical editor, so no slot or comman
d seam owns them. This plugin therefore:

- registers an invisible Session-scoped occupant in `conversation.composer.dock`;
- reads the Sessio
n's Chat nodes through the standard `useChat` hook (`snapshot.nodes`) and the draft through the stan

dard `useInput` hook;
- writes the recalled text through the standard `inputActions.setDraft` API, s

o the edit stays part of the composer's own draft history;
- watches the key on two paths: a documen
t-level `keydown` listener and the shortcuts service's `observeFixedInput` seam. The document listen
er runs after the composer's own keymap, so a slash menu or an IME that already handled the key stil
l wins; the fixed-input seam covers compositions where a native Desktop adapter owns the DOM feed. E
xactly one path acts, because the first one to act cancels the event.
Replacing a draft commits paragraph by paragraph, so intermediate empty or partial drafts are expect
ed; the plugin treats a published draft that matches what it wrote (ignoring whitespace) as its own
and keeps browse mode. Only a genuinely visible slash/reference menu (a mounted `role="listbox"`), a
n IME composition, or a held modifier keeps the key — a caret move the editor already marked as hand
led does not. Editing keys (Backspace, Delete, Enter, printable characters, Ctrl+V/Ctrl+X) end brows
e mode; navigation keys and shortcuts such as Ctrl+C do not. The browse state machine itself is cach
ed per composer editor element, so re-rendering or remounting the dock entry never drops the browse
state or the remembered draft, and starting browse again from an already-recalled message never over
writes the draft you were writing — walking past the newest message always lands on that draft, a bl
ank composer included. When the host re-seeds a stale stored draft over a restore, the plugin re-ass
erts the restored text (the counter-punch yields only to genuine text editing, not to arrow keys), a
nd every handled key re-arms that defense for the text it just published.

## Relationship to other plugins
The npm name `dsh-input-history` is already taken by a different community plugin that also recalls
prompts with ↑/↓. The two differ in mechanism and behaviour:
| | dsh-composer-input-history (this plugin) | dsh-input-history |
| History source | the Session transcript the Chat view already loads | a separate local store of su

bmitted prompts |
| Non-empty draft | recalls and remembers the draft, restoring it below the newest

message | recalls only from an empty composer |
| Attachments | not part of the recalled text | per

sists and re-attaches them |
[该节后续省略]
## Compatibility
Developed and verified against `@deepseek-ai/dsh` `0.2.0-rc.2`. The plugin uses only documented seam
s: `ctx.slots`, the Session standard props (`useChat`, `useInput`, `inputActions`), `ctx.shortcuts.o
bserveFixedInput`, and the activation context's `uiSession` binding source (declared in `dsh.client.
inject`). It declares `dsh.client.inject` on `dsh-client-ui-conversation`, `dsh-client-ui-chat`, and
`dsh-client-shortcuts` so activation order is deterministic.
## Limitations

- History is per Session. Cross-session recall (recent Sessions' inputs) is not implemented yet.
- H
istory reflects the loaded transcript window plus the persisted per-Session record; a message never

seen by this plugin (sent while it was uninstalled) is not recalled.
- The recalled text is plain te

xt: reference chips and attachments from the original message are not restored.
- One resident compo

ser per Web page is assumed, matching the shell's own design.
- On the home screen (no Session open)
there is no recall: the composer dock only renders inside a session.
